query: Which method can be used for phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A data-driven machine-learning approach (e.g., Bayesian optimization) can systematically identify optimal mechanical alloying and sintering parameters that simultaneously ensure targeted phase stability, refined microstructure, and enhanced mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy or complex concentrated alloy in powder form, ready for consolidation by processes such as mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
generation.intervention: Apply Bayesian optimization (or a comparable ML framework) to explore composition and processing parameters (e.g., milling time, sintering temperature, applied pressure) and optimize for stable phases, fine-grained microstructures, and higher mechanical performance.
generation.conditions: Use methodical, iterative coupling of automated experiments, microstructural characterization, and mechanical testing to train surrogate models that predict and guide parameter selection.
generation.structural_mediator: Controlled precipitation and stable phase formation, as well as grain boundary pinning from reinforcement phases or refined grains influencing mechanical properties.
generation.mechanism: The ML model rapidly correlates composition, processing, and microstructure with mechanical properties, enabling targeted refinements and accelerated discovery of optimal process windows.
generation.predicted_outcome: Substantial enhancement over standard heuristics-based process design, with potential increases in yield strength of up to ~10–20% and improved ductility at room or elevated temperatures.
generation.baseline: Traditional trial-and-error or single-parameter-at-a-time optimization approaches for mechanical alloying and sintering.
generation.boundary: Results may vary considerably depending on alloy composition and downstream thermomechanical treatments; further validation is needed for large compositional ranges or non-laboratory conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of property improvements remains to be experimentally verified; performance gains could deviate if the ML models are extrapolated beyond the studied parameter domain.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a multi-step experimental campaign comparing an ML-guided process parameter selection to a conventional trial-and-error approach for a candidate high-entropy alloy powder via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
measurements: Grain size distribution via electron microscopy

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If statistically significant improvements (e.g., >10% in yield strength and refined microstructure) are not achieved by the ML-guided process over the conventional approach, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Discovering novel high entropy alloys (HEAs) with exceptional performance has ushered in a new era for materials design [1] – [3] . The melting temperature is a crucial parameter in the search for such materials. For instance, a correlation between a high melting point and elevated temperature strength has been identified in refractory complex concentrated alloys [4] . Besides the melting temperature, other melting properties, such as enthalpy and entropy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point, are also crucial for constructing phase diagrams and developing novel materials. However, experimental measurements on these properties, even for unary refractory materials, face severe challenges due to high melting points, often resulting in very scattered experimental data, if available at all. Additionally, the vast compositional space of HEAs makes systematic experimental screening of promising candidates impractical.

Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties

The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

decision.trend: Earlier investigations on high-entropy alloys (HEAs) and refractory HEAs have demonstrated that advanced powder-based or severe plastic deformation-based routes can refine microstructure, improve densification, and elevate mechanical or functional properties. For instance, mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering (PMC5978046) achieved submicrometer-scale grain sizes and enhanced yield strengths, while friction processing (PMC9026100) refined grain sizes down to below 1 μm, improving high-temperature oxidation resistance. However, controlling phase stability under diverse service conditions and mapping the interplay of processing parameters with microstructure-property evolution remains challenging.
decision.unsolved: Methods for simultaneously stabilizing desired phases, achieving controlled grain refinement, and optimizing multiple properties still rely heavily on trial-and-error. A more systematic, predictive approach is needed to correlate processing steps (e.g., milling time, sintering or friction processing parameters) with the resulting microstructure and performance.
decision.lever: Employ a Bayesian optimization or similar ML approach to identify optimal mechanical alloying/sintering/friction-processing parameters that simultaneously stabilize target phases, refine grains, and enhance properties. Key levers include defining ML-based surrogate models for the composition-processing-property space and employing high-throughput or automated experiments to refine model predictions.
decision.why: Empirical tuning of complex, multi-step manufacturing routes has proven both time-consuming and uncertain. A data-driven strategy leveraging machine learning can efficiently navigate the large parameter space of HEA processing, accelerate discovery of the best process windows, and systematically optimize phase stability, microstructure development, and overall material performance.
